unsupervised-learning.name: Unsupervised Learning
unsupervised-learning.bio: Podcast: Ep 87: Gemini Co-Lead on World Models, RL's Next Domains & Continual Learning

html_en:
From iterative model improvements to self-improving agents, today's developments reveal an industry doubling down on capability enhancement and user-centric design. The conversation isn't just about making AI faster—it's about making it genuinely useful.

The Speed Race Heats Up

The competitive dynamics around AI performance took center stage today, with Thomas Sottiaux celebrating a milestone and signaling what's to come. Announcing five million users, he promised to reset limits "to celebrate" and invited everyone to go "/fast." But perhaps more revealing was his explanation of OpenAI's versioning strategy:
"When we go from GPT-5.0 -> GPT-5.1 -> ... -> GPT-5.5, the number incrementing goes with improvements in capabilities and token efficiency (which translates to speed gains). With GPT-5.5 our best model yet. A simple strategy that we would like to continue."
This incremental improvement philosophy contrasts sharply with the traditional "big model drop" approach. It suggests a maturation in the field—less about revolutionary leaps, more about consistent, measurable progress that users can actually feel. The sentiment was echoed by Peter Steinberger, who noted how recent improvements have transformed his workflow: "With GPT 5.5, /goal, autoreview and crabbox my prompts moved from ~30-60min to often 4-10h tasks and my confidence that it's ready is much much higher."

AI as Product Philosophy, Not Technology Crutch

Guillermo Rauch cut through the AI hype with refreshing clarity: "Ship the best product. Use lots of AI, some AI, maybe no AI. Just be the best." This perspective aligns with Aaron Levie's observations from the enterprise trenches. In a detailed thread, he pushed back against the job displacement narrative:
"Most businesses have been constrained by how much software they can produce at a given cost, how many sales reps they can hire, how many marketing campaigns they can run... When AI makes it possible to do more of this, investment goes back into the business."
Levie's insight—that AI is creating expansion rather than contraction in business capabilities—suggests we're seeing the early stages of a productivity renaissance rather than a job apocalypse.

The Agent Evolution: Self-Improvement Meets Real Deployment

Anthropic made waves with their latest Claude Managed Agents update, introducing "dreaming"—a feature that lets agents review past sessions to find patterns and improve over time. The concept is elegant: agents that don't just execute tasks but learn from their collective experience across sessions. The real-world applications are already impressive. Harvey uses the system for complex legal work, seeing "completion rates go up ~6x" thanks to agents that remember filetype workarounds between sessions. Netflix's platform team built analysis agents that process logs from hundreds of builds in parallel, using multiagent orchestration to surface only the patterns worth acting on. What's particularly notable is the emphasis on "outcomes"—structured evaluation that lets agents self-correct against defined success criteria. As Anthropic puts it: "Agents do their best work when they know what 'good' looks like." This mirrors observations from the developer community about AI code review. Steinberger noted a fascinating pattern: "Ask it to review code for bugs and it will tell you all good, tell it there is a bug and it will LOOP AND LOOP and will find issues."

Multimodal Models: The Search for the "GPT Moment"

In a revealing conversation on Unsupervised Learning, Gemini co-lead Oriol Vinyals offered candid insights into the current state of multimodal AI. While acknowledging Google's advances with models like Omni, he admitted:
"The GPT moment of video and images, I'm not sure we quite have seen that... Could we train on all the videos ever produced and images and get to the same level of understanding that clearly the language models using language get to? Probably not."
This honesty about current limitations is refreshing. Vinyals described the core challenge: linking visual understanding to conceptual knowledge without explicit language bridging. The dream of training on raw visual data and deriving physical laws—like learning gravity from watching objects fall—remains just that: a dream. Yet the progress is undeniable. Omni demonstrates sophisticated video understanding and editing capabilities that feel "almost magical," as Vinyals put it. The question isn't whether we'll crack this puzzle, but when.

The Human Element in an AI World

Perhaps the most touching moment came from Peter Yang's observation about education: "Just spent an hour with daughter learning CS 101 from @brilliantorg. She doesn't want to give up until she beats Joyce B 🔥" His follow-up insight captures something profound about AI's potential: "Basically the ultimate education app is you're playing Final Fantasy or something and you're learning math and CS at the same time." This vision—AI as an engaging, game-like tutor that makes learning irresistible—may be where the technology's true promise lies. Not in replacing human connection, but in amplifying it through better tools and experiences. As the industry races toward ever-more-capable systems, these glimpses of AI enhancing rather than replacing human endeavor offer the most compelling glimpse of our shared future.
html_zh:
大模型的进化正在从单纯的性能提升转向更复杂的能力整合，从OpenAI的Codex迭代策略到Anthropic的自我改进代理，一个更加智能化的AI生态正在形成。

模型迭代的新策略

OpenAI的Codex团队分享了他们对模型版本迭代的思考。Thomas Sottiaux透露了一个颇为简洁的发展策略：

"当我们从GPT-5.0 -> GPT-5.1 -> ... -> GPT-5.5时，版本号的递增伴随着能力和token效率的提升（这转化为速度增益）。GPT-5.5是我们迄今为止最好的模型。这是一个我们希望继续的简单策略。"

更令人兴奋的是，Codex团队宣布将重置用户使用限制来庆祝五百万用户里程碑，显示出对产品成熟度的信心。用户体验的持续优化也是重点，团队正在征询社区反馈，寻找那些"长期未修复且令人烦恼"的问题。

AI代理的自我改进革命

Anthropic今天发布了Claude Managed Agents的重大更新，引入了"梦境"（dreaming）功能——一种让AI代理能够回顾过往会话、发现模式并自我改进的机制。

这项创新的核心在于让代理系统具备长期学习能力：

"梦境是一个定期过程，它回顾您的代理会话和内存存储，提取模式，并整理记忆，让您的代理随时间改进。您可以决定控制程度：梦境可以自动更新内存，或者您可以在变更生效前进行审查。"

该更新还包括了结果导向（outcomes）和多代理编排（multiagent orchestration）功能。Netflix的平台团队已经在使用多代理编排来并行分析数百个构建的日志，而Harvey则利用梦境功能让法律文档代理在会话间保持学习，完成率提升了约6倍。

世界模型：通往AGI的另一条路径

在最新一期的Unsupervised Learning播客中，Gemini联合负责人Oriol Vinyals深入探讨了Google在世界模型方面的独特路径。

与其他实验室专注于代码和递归自我改进不同，Google将多模态理解视为核心策略：

"自第一天起，早在Gemini项目启动之前，我们就在研究不仅仅是语言，还要理解视觉世界，在视觉、盲视频等背景下联合建模词汇。"

Vinyals认为，尽管在多模态融合方面取得了显著进展，但真正的"GPT时刻"——即从纯视频和图像数据中提取深层理解——仍未到来。他提出了一个富有挑战性的愿景：

"能否仅从图像中精确描述世界如何运作？在那里，将语言或我们有时称为的概念与您在图像中看到的内容联系起来，而没有明确的语言链接，这是相当棘手的。"

开发工具的智能化转型

AI正在重塑软件开发的每个环节。Peter Steinberger分享了他使用GPT 5.5、自动审查和相关工具的体验：

"我的提示从大约30-60分钟的任务变成了经常是4-10小时的任务，而我对其准备就绪的信心要高得多。让代理产出结果是一项技能。"

Ryan Lu特别赞赏Cursor的自动审查功能：

"我喜欢自动审查的地方在于：Cursor解释命令和风险，让新编码者更容易学习和做事。"

这种工具智能化的趋势也体现在产品战略上。Guillermo Rauch提出了一个清晰的产品哲学：

"发布最好的产品。大量使用AI、适度使用AI、或许不使用AI。只要做到最好。"

企业AI采用的现实图景

Aaron Levie分享了企业AI采用的真实情况，挑战了AI将大规模裁员的传统观点：

"在我与大企业CIO、CTO和CEO的大多数对话中，他们要么因为AI而增长（在FDE、工程等新职能岗位），要么至少将效率节省重新投资到业务的新领域（销售、市场营销等）。"

他引用高盛CEO David Solomon的观点，认为AI繁荣既在创造全新的就业机会，也在释放资金投资到以前资金不足或因AI而需求增加的领域。这种观点为理解AI对经济影响提供了更加乐观和现实的视角。
